abstract.p: This paper describes the submission of the HITS team to the DISRPT 2025 shared task. The shared task includes three sub-tasks: (1) discourse unit segmentation across formalisms, (2) cross-lingual discourse connective identification, and (3) cross-formalism discourse relation classification. For task (1), we use the google/mt5-xl model as our base model. Additionally, we combine the weighted crossentropy loss function and adversarial training techniques. For task (2), we propose an ensemble of three encoder models whose embeddings are fused together with multi-head attention. We also integrate linguistic features and employ a CRF layer with label smoothing and focal loss to further improve performance. Finally for task (3), we introduce a two-stage curriculum learning framework with knowledge distillation. A smaller "student" model internalizes a larger "teacher" model's reasoning by first learning simple label prediction and then learning to analyze Chain-of-Thought explanations before the label prediction for more difficult samples.
